reconstruction.retention: Pointer-bearing inputs are promoted to shared graphs; result may reconstruct aggregates or alias input.
reconstruction.teardown: Managed graphs remain tracing-owned until unreachable; partial managed construction is reclaimed by tracing. C scratch requires separate runtime cleanup.
reconstruction.eligibility: Requires tracing; no deterministic graph or partial-construction ownership claim.

retained_runtime.retention: Callbacks, cached values and contextual inputs may outlive calls; complete reachable graphs remain shared.
retained_runtime.teardown: Runtime completion/close/scoped restoration handles external storage where verified; managed captured/result graphs require tracing after runtime roots disappear.
retained_runtime.eligibility: Requires tracing; retained contexts and cycles need separate proofs before tracing-free eligibility.

scalar_or_leaf.retention: Unknown contract retains conservative sharing for pointer-bearing inputs; scalar words are not reference-counted.
scalar_or_leaf.teardown: Scalar results require no managed destruction; any fresh/aliased leaf or wrapper remains tracing-owned.
scalar_or_leaf.eligibility: Requires tracing at this boundary until its actual monomorphic result and retention are proved.

numeric_runtime.retention: Descriptor-based arrays, numeric wrappers and kernel inputs retain unknown-boundary sharing. Scalar results alone do not prove payload or backing-storage ownership.
numeric_runtime.teardown: Managed results/backing graphs require tracing; explicit tape/device/external storage must follow its separately verified runtime lifetime.
numeric_runtime.eligibility: Requires tracing; natural-width representation and view owners remain phase3 tasks.
